## TL;DR - AI absorbs RAM and memory allocated to data centers - In Switzerland, some models are unavailable or much more expensive - MediaMarkt reports average price increases of 40% to 120% - Interdiscount expects stable availability in the coming months
## Key facts - Cause → global demand for RAM and storage systems - Products → notebooks, desktop PCs, tablets and smartphones - Fust → growing scarcity since mid-2026 - MediaMarkt → procurement difficulties since late 2025 - Prices → average increases of 40% to 120% since the start of the chip crisis - Interdiscount → sporadic shortages of processors and high-capacity memory
In Lugano, anyone who has saved money for a new mobile phone or needs to retire their laptop may face two problems: the model is unavailable, or the configuration with more memory costs several hundred francs more. The difficulty affects stores and online platforms, and the phenomenon has also reached Switzerland.
The explanation given is global: the strong expansion of data centers dedicated to artificial intelligence is absorbing RAM and storage systems. Demand for these components is said to be driven by the growth of AI, while an increasing share of production is said to be destined for data centers and the infrastructure they require. For PCs, notebooks and other devices, the result is less certain availability, with repercussions for the choice of models and configurations.
### A problem that starts with the components
Retailers describe a situation that is not uniform. Interdiscount reports sporadic shortages of certain processors and high-capacity memory modules across the market. The difficulty varies depending on the model and configuration; according to the company, the most delicate point is the dynamics of supply and prices. The forecast communicated is for stable availability in the coming months.
Fust reports observing, since mid-2026, growing scarcity of notebooks, desktop PCs and devices with high memory capacities. It does not yet speak of a general interruption, but of longer restocking times and rising prices.
MediaMarkt dates the difficulties to late 2025. The first reports, it explains, concerned Windows OEM manufacturers and then Apple. In its assessment, the problem is not limited to notebooks and PCs: it also includes smartphones. For those looking for a phone, comparing offerte mobile therefore does not replace checking the device's availability.
The three responses show a non-uniform market: for some components, the shortage remains sporadic; for others, lead times are getting longer, while price pressure is affecting more categories. The situation affects notebooks, desktop PCs, tablets and smartphones, but with intensity linked to the configuration. For Swiss consumers, the comparison cannot stop at the device name. Retailers' responses link availability and price to manufacturer, model, processor, memory and configuration. The same product family can therefore present different conditions when the required capacity changes.
### Capacity becomes the decisive variable
MediaMarkt observes that those who only want to browse online and reply to emails often do not need 16 GB of RAM. Likewise, for many uses, a 256 or 512 GB SSD may be sufficient instead of 1 TB. The assessment should be made before paying the premium for a higher-capacity configuration, without automatically considering the minimum capacity suitable for every need.
Companies are reacting in different ways. Interdiscount focuses on forward-looking planning and alternative configurations. Fust speaks of proactive inventory management, diversification among distributors and advance volume planning; if a model is unavailable, it proposes equivalent alternative configurations. MediaMarkt orders larger quantities in advance because it expects price increases on a quarterly basis, thereby maintaining more advantageous prices for a longer period.
For buyers, the practical consequence is that the alternative is not simply to wait or give up. You can ask whether the problem concerns the exact model, the processor, the RAM or the SSD storage, and assess an equivalent configuration. This distinction is also relevant for smartphones, which MediaMarkt includes among the affected products.
The time factor should also be viewed with caution. Interdiscount expects stable availability in the coming months; Fust, on the other hand, reports significantly longer restocking times and rising prices. MediaMarkt links its ordering policy to quarterly price increases. These indications do not produce a single answer valid for everyone: waiting may mean finding more choice according to one forecast, but it does not guarantee spending less.
The responses collected do not indicate a certain window for Black Friday or Cyber Monday and do not set a purchase date valid for everyone. For a family or a worker, the expense must therefore be included in planning for costo della vita in Svizzera: the price to compare is that of the configuration actually needed, not that of the highest-capacity model seen online.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. The most practical way to approach the market described by the retailers is to turn the research into a configuration check, rather than a hunt for the commercial name alone. The process can be applied to notebooks, desktop PCs, tablets and smartphones, categories mentioned in the responses.
### Five checks before ordering
1. Start with the actual use. If the need is to browse online and respond to emails, consider MediaMarkt's indication regarding configurations with 16 GB of RAM and a 1 TB SSD. The assessment should be made before settling on a higher capacity.
2. Write down the requirements for the model you are looking for: processor, RAM, SSD capacity and overall configuration. The shortages reported by Interdiscount in fact vary precisely according to the model and configuration.
3. Check availability both in stores and online. A model may not be available in a specific configuration, while the retailer may offer an alternative. Therefore, do not stop at the series name: check the device's complete specifications.
4. If the exact configuration is not available, ask for an equivalent proposal. Interdiscount indicates alternative configurations, Fust equivalent alternatives and MediaMarkt also simpler configurations to keep products in different price ranges.
5. Compare the timing of the purchase with the signals from the retailers. Interdiscount expects stable availability over the coming months; Fust reports longer lead times and rising prices; MediaMarkt orders in advance in anticipation of quarterly increases. These are factors to consider alongside the price of the chosen configuration.
Before concluding, note down the model, processor, RAM, storage space, price and availability. The same check applies to a smartphone, because MediaMarkt also includes this category among the supply difficulties. This way, the search remains anchored to the features that are genuinely necessary and not merely to the highest capacity offered.

## TL;DR - The 2026 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences will be announced on October 12 - Ernst Fehr is among the possible winners - Clarivate has named four economists - Polymarket estimates Fehr at 6%
## Key facts - Prize → 2026 Nobel Prize in Economics - Announcement → Monday, October 12 - Candidate → Ernst Fehr, Swiss-Austrian economist - Polymarket → Ariel Pakes 19%, Ernst Fehr 6% - Institute → UBS International Center of Economics in Society - Academic recognition → USI honorary doctorate in 2009
The winner of the 2026 Nobel Prize in Economics will be announced on Monday, October 12. Ernst Fehr, a Swiss-Austrian economist and professor at the University of Zurich, remains among the possible recipients.
The 70-year-old has been considered a possible winner for years, but is not among the leading favorites. Predicting the choice remains difficult: the Nobel Foundation keeps the names of the candidates secret, and decisions from previous years offer few clues about the committee's intentions.
### The scientific profile
Fehr is one of the leading figures in behavioral economics, which examines the processes underlying individual economic decisions. His studies have helped cast doubt on the traditional model of “Homo oeconomicus,” which portrays individuals as guided exclusively by self-interest.
The studies cited by the source show instead that fairness, justice and the well-being of others also factor into choices. For this reason, Fehr is among the most cited economists in the German-speaking world.
Since 2012, he has headed the UBS International Center of Economics in Society, an institute affiliated with the University of Zurich and established thanks to an initial funding of 100 million Swiss francs from UBS bank. Fehr has assured that the institute's scientific independence is “completely guaranteed.”
His relationship with the Swiss university system also includes Università della Svizzera italiana: in 2009, USI awarded him an honorary doctorate.
His international reputation was on display last June: a conference held in Zurich to celebrate his 70th birthday was attended by several Nobel laureates, including Abhijit Banerjee, Esther Duflo, Joel Mokyr, Oliver Hart and Jean Tirole.
Clarivate did not include the economist among the names highlighted for 2026. The company selects researchers based on the scientific impact reflected in citations of their work; the source nevertheless specifies that the list does not constitute an official prediction of the award.
The picture therefore remains open, with Fehr still among the possible winners but outside the group of leading favorites. The decision will be made public only with the announcement scheduled for Monday, October 12.
Unlike the other five Nobel Prizes, this award was not provided for in Alfred Nobel's will. For the Swiss public, the point is not to turn every signal into a prediction, but to distinguish the sources accompanying the race for the prize. The source presents three: Clarivate's selection, the Polymarket prediction market, and the announcement by the Nobel committee.
### Three signals, three levels of reliability
| Signal | Reported data | Correct interpretation | |---|---|---| | Clarivate | Michael Woodford, Columbia University, monetary theory and central bank communication; Susan Athey, Stanford, and Hal Varian, Berkeley, economics of information technologies; Sidney Winter, Pennsylvania, evolutionary economics and firms' adaptation. | Unofficial selection | | Polymarket | Ariel Pakes, Harvard, 19%; Ernst Fehr, sixth, 6%. | Speculative assessments, not the committee's decision | | Announcement | Monday, October 12, winner of the 2026 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences. | Outcome to await |
Clarivate's list brings together names selected on the basis of scientific impact measured by citations. Therefore, Fehr's absence does not amount to a rejection, and the presence of the four economists does not amount to an official shortlist from the Nobel committee.
The second signal comes from a market in which users can bet on the award. Ariel Pakes, a Harvard economist specializing in empirical market analysis, is listed at 19%; Fehr is sixth at 6%. The source describes these assessments as speculative: they do not necessarily reflect the committee's decision.
For those reading the news from Switzerland, this distinction avoids assigning excessive meaning to a percentage. The 6% describes the position indicated by Polymarket at that moment, not an official figure from the Nobel Foundation nor an outcome already decided.
The possible award for studies on the digital economy introduces another perspective. Clarivate links Athey and Varian to the economics of information technologies; recognition in this area would be significant given the growing importance of online platforms, data, and artificial intelligence. The source, however, presents it as a possibility.

## TL;DR - Late September: attack on Publica's software provider - Names, AHV numbers and salaries among the data at risk - Publica has 66’000 active insured persons and 40’000 pension recipients - Pension funds were not affected
## Key facts - Institution → Publica, the Swiss Confederation's pension fund - Provider → PK Softech AG - Timing → late September - Potentially affected → approximately 66’000 active insured persons and 40’000 pension beneficiaries - Investigation → Office of the Attorney General of Switzerland - Funds → not affected and safe, according to Publica
At the end of September, a cyberattack hit an external software provider of Publica, the Swiss Confederation's pension fund. The incident caused a data breach and, according to current findings, may have involved particularly sensitive personal information.
The case became public on Thursday, after Publica sent a notice to the insured. The document, seen by SRF, indicates that personal data were probably stolen. Beatrice Rychen, spokesperson for the pension institution, described what happened in stark terms: «For us, this is the worst thing that could have happened».
The information that may have been obtained includes first and last names, dates of birth, AHV numbers, addresses, private and business telephone numbers, as well as personal and business email addresses. The list also includes pension data, such as salary and pension assets, marital status and information relating to a spouse or partner.
### The route via the external provider
It is not yet clear whether the leak concerns all approximately 66’000 active insured persons and 40’000 pension beneficiaries, or only some of them. Publica does clarify, however, that the pension funds were not affected and are safe.
The cybercriminals did not attack the Swiss Confederation's pension fund directly. The target was PK Softech AG, the external company that develops applications for pension funds. Through this provider, the perpetrators are believed to have gained access to Publica's data.
The Office of the Attorney General of Switzerland is investigating the case. In the meantime, specialists are analyzing the stolen information. It is not known whether the attack also involved data from other pension institutions. For anyone checking their own situation, the AHV number entry is therefore one of the categories to distinguish from investments and funds, which Publica says were not affected. The guide on previdenza AVS may help with navigating pension terminology. ### Two distinct risks for insured persons
The matter has two distinct dimensions. The first concerns the possible theft of personal data; the second concerns pension funds. Publica says the funds are safe, while warning of a risk to individuals linked to the misuse of the information.
The theft of a name, address, AHV number, salary or pension assets could, according to the institution, be used in an attempt to assume other people's identities or to gain an advantage. The risk mentioned does not, however, mean that unlawful use of the data has already been established. Specialists are still analyzing how much was stolen.
| Scenario | What the source indicates | Practical interpretation | |---|---|---| | Only some of the insured persons are involved | The scope has not been clarified | Not everyone affected would necessarily be exposed | | All insured persons and beneficiaries are involved | The possibility has not been ruled out | The scope would be broader, but this has not been confirmed | | Pension funds | Publica says they are safe | The news concerns data, not a declared loss of funds |
The reference to salary also makes it important to interpret correctly any salary information that may be contained in the stolen data. For this reason, it may be useful to consult busta paga svizzera, without confusing a category of personal data with a movement in the pension account.
The attack bears similarities to the one that involved Xplain in 2023: in that case, cybercriminals had gained access to information from federal offices through an external software company, resulting in the theft of approximately 1,3 million sensitive files. Two years ago, at the end of an administrative investigation, the Federal Council had adopted measures to prevent further thefts at IT providers. Since then, cooperation with external companies has also been subject to additional security requirements.
The precedent does not automatically make it possible to determine the scope of the Publica case. It does, however, show why the software provider, although not the Confederation's pension fund, is the central focus of the investigation.

item.title: Geneva–Fribourg, a railway route under pressure
item.description: Thirteen disruptions on the line since the beginning of the year More than 150’000 passengers and over 700 trains every day Burnt cables, damaged tracks and a bird
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Thirteen disruptions on the line since the beginning of the year - Over 150’000 passengers and more than 700 trains every day - Burnt cables, damaged tracks and a bird among the causes - Léman 2030 expands the stations in Lausanne and Geneva
## Key facts - Line → Geneva-Fribourg - Disruptions → thirteen since the beginning of the year - Daily traffic → over 150’000 passengers and more than 700 trains - Causes → burnt cables, damaged tracks, short circuit caused by a bird - Programme → Léman 2030 - New line → Morges-Perroy
Thirteen disruptions since the beginning of the year have affected the railway line between Geneva and Fribourg. Each incident started with a failure at a strategic point and halted traffic on a route that carries over 150’000 passengers every day and sees more than 700 trains pass through.
The causes of the incidents varied: cables caught fire, tracks were damaged and a bird even caused a short circuit. For passengers, however, the outcome was similar: delays and cancellations, with few alternatives when the line is blocked. The frustration, the source reports, is palpable among those who say they have already experienced several service disruptions.
### The reliability bottleneck
Among the incidents mentioned are the track damage attributed to the Servette ultras in Lausanne. The case adds to a sequence in which the source of the problem changes, while the consequence for rail traffic remains the same. For those who need to plan a journey, the issue is therefore not only the technical cause of the failure, but also the difficulty of quickly finding a replacement for the route.
The pressure is also evident on board. During peak hours, it is not always possible to find a seat; in the morning and evening, trains are often full. The line thus combines two distinct problems: disruption when a failure occurs and overcrowding when the service continues.
According to FFS, not all disruptions are caused by its operations. Linus Looser, Head of Infrastructure at Swiss Federal Railways, explains: > «Every day, the line sees over 150’000 passengers and more than 700 trains pass through. Disruptions are no more frequent than elsewhere, but they have a greater impact: without alternative routes, a single failure can bring the entire line to a standstill and have a major impact on customers.»
Over the past twenty years, the number of passengers has tripled. The infrastructure response includes the Léman 2030 programme, with the expansion of the stations in Lausanne and Geneva, and the new line between Morges and Perroy, the first step towards greater capacity between Lausanne and Geneva. For those consulting mezzi pubblici, the article therefore describes a route where demand, overcrowding and vulnerability of rail traffic combine. ## What changes for those who use the route
The practical reading of the situation starts with a distinction: reliability and capacity are related but not identical problems. A fault at a strategic point can bring the line to a standstill because there are not enough alternative routes; when the trains are running, however, the number of passengers and the growth recorded translate into trains that are often full. Solving one problem does not automatically eliminate the other.
### Three pressures to separate

## TL;DR - 80% of vacancies are filled by local staff. - Direct hiring from abroad accounts for about 20%. - Family accommodation with a home office can cost 6000 CHF. - In urban centers, vacant housing is extremely scarce.
## Key facts - Vacant positions filled locally → 80% - Direct hires from abroad → approximately 20% - Interviewee → Christian Atkinson - Company → Robert Walters - Family accommodation with a home office → can quickly reach 6000 francs per month - City of residence → Zurich
80% of vacancies in Switzerland are filled by local staff. Christian Atkinson, who coordinates Robert Walters' Swiss personnel consultancy activities, emphasizes this to put into perspective the idea that companies primarily look across the border for highly qualified professionals.
According to the headhunter, when a company has to fill a position, it starts with the domestic market. It looks for people already rooted in the country, with suitable qualifications and knowledge of the local work culture. Direct hires from abroad perhaps account for 20%. For the employer, the risk is real: a candidate may withdraw at the last moment, visa procedures may drag on, or integration may not work. In that case, whoever has arrived leaves at the first opportunity.
The high salary remains an attraction, but it is not enough to explain the choice. Atkinson describes an enormous costo della vita in Svizzera capable of reducing the salary advantage. After the first bills for rent and health insurance, actual savings may turn out to be almost the same as those attainable, for example, in the United Kingdom. For this reason, anyone who changes jobs exclusively for the salary is, in his view, a warning sign.
### Rent, family and first impressions
Housing is now companies' main concern and the most stressful factor for those who want to relocate. In urban centers, the vacancy rate is extremely low; many expats have to move several times during the first few months. For a family, an apartment with a dedicated home office space can quickly cost up to 6000 francs per month.
Atkinson, 46, lives with his family in Zurich. Raised in the United Kingdom, he says that upon his arrival he booked an Airbnb on Langstrasse, when he had an infant: the choice placed him in the middle of a nightlife district. The episode explains why, in his view, without someone capable of guiding newcomers, people easily make wrong decisions. Switzerland remains attractive for its safety, nature, quality of life and environment for children, but relocation requires stronger motivations than mere earnings. ## The sector changes the value of the offer
The same professional offer does not carry the same weight for everyone. Atkinson distinguishes mainly between IT, finance and pharmaceuticals, and also links the assessment to the age of those relocating. The comparison therefore concerns not only the figure on the payslip, but the way work fits into everyday life.
| Profile | Element that attracts or puts off | | IT | Specialists ask for broad opportunities to work remotely; in Switzerland, being present in the office often remains the rule. | | Finance | More agile corporate structures than in London are an attraction. | | Pharmaceuticals | The Basel region is described as a natural draw. | | Younger people | The policy on free movement and the social climate carry weight. | | Older people | The choice focuses more on school and family. |
For those looking in annunci di lavoro, the first practical comparison is therefore between job duties and work organization. In the IT sector, recruitment from abroad becomes more difficult when specialists ask for broad opportunities to work remotely and office presence remains strong in Switzerland. Atkinson cites Germany, where salaries are lower but models are often more flexible. In finance, by contrast, the identified lever is the agility of corporate structures compared with London. For pharmaceuticals, the geographical reference is the Basel region.
The most unexpected difference may emerge as early as preschool. In the United Kingdom, Atkinson explains, nursery school focuses on academic learning from the outset. In a Swiss preschool, his son told him that he had learned to light matches and fend for himself in the woods: it was a shock for his father.
Behind the episode lies a different educational philosophy. The model described by Atkinson promotes autonomy and individual responsibility; academic achievement, in his experience, evens out later. His children grew up happy, healthy and extremely independent. For an international family, the question to ask is not only what salary to expect, but what view of childhood and schooling one will encounter after the move.
Language, too, should be considered without making assumptions. The Swiss approach to languages is open and, in many international companies, English is more than sufficient. This can facilitate entry into professional life, but it does not eliminate the other obstacles to integration mentioned in the interview. The choice therefore depends on the combination of work, age and family, not on a single ranking of attractiveness.

The decision can be turned into an orderly assessment, without treating salary as the only variable. The criteria that emerged from the interview help prepare a choice less exposed to errors.
### Four practical steps
1. Clarify the motivation. Before responding to an offer, write down what you are looking for beyond money: security, contact with nature, quality of life and an environment favorable to children. If salary is the only reason for the change, the interview suggests considering this motivation a warning sign.
2. Calculate the real margin. Set net salary alongside the first expenses cited by Atkinson: rent and cassa malati. The comparison must concern what remains for savings, investments or retirement, not the isolated salary figure. The assessment also serves to measure the difference compared with the situation in the United Kingdom, given as a point of comparison in the interview.
3. Prepare the home search. Define the family's needs immediately, including space for a home office, and do not choose an address without understanding its surroundings. The Airbnb experience on Langstrasse shows the risk of a decision made without guidance. Since many expats change accommodation several times in the first few months, the housing search should be treated as part of the professional decision.
4. Check work and school together. Ask how much office presence the role requires and how compatible the arrangement is with family needs. Then compare expectations regarding early childhood education: the Swiss system described by Atkinson prioritizes independence and responsibility, while the British experience starts with a more academic focus. The question is not which model is better, but which one is suitable for the children.
If one assessment remains open, it is advisable to pause the comparison and formulate a precise question for the company or the family: the transfer must hold up together in terms of work, housing and educational expectations. 988'700 tonnes of cement were delivered in Switzerland in the third quarter, 1% more than in the same period last year. The news was reported by Keystone-ATS and reflects a slight increase in the flow of supplies.
### Moderate growth, with demand still present
Over the first nine months, growth stood at a similar 1%, for a total of 2,8 million tonnes. The quarterly and cumulative figures therefore describe the same trend: quantities delivered increased, without the source reporting a larger change.
Cemsuisse, the industry association, writes in a statement that “Swiss quality cement continues to be in high demand.” On the path toward the goal of net-zero emissions, the association adds, the sector shows a strong propensity for innovation and makes significant investments to reduce the CO2 released by its products.
In recent years, demand for more environmentally friendly types of cement has continued to grow. Today, low-clinker types account for over 98% of the total volume delivered. Portland cement, used exclusively until the 1990s, represents only a marginal 1% share.
Cemsuisse presents the composition of supplies as a dual result: the sector makes an important contribution to the domestic supply of cement and concrete and supports the Confederation’s climate policy objectives.
From a logistics perspective, the tables published by the organization founded in 1881 indicate that 32% of deliveries in the January–September period took place by rail, compared with 68% by road. The rail share also fell by more than two percentage points in the comparison reported. Cemsuisse links this figure to problems with single-wagonload transport, which force companies to resort to trucks. Director Stefan Vannoni expresses the sector’s regret, while the organization reports that it has already repeatedly flagged the shortcomings of rail freight transport to the competent authorities. ## What the data indicate for the Swiss system
### Volume, product and transport are three different dimensions
To read the press release without confusing the levels, it is helpful to separate the quantity delivered, the type of cement and the means used to distribute it. These are three indicators present in the same picture, but they describe different aspects of the industry's activity.

The second figure concerns the composition. The clear predominance of cements with a low clinker content, exceeding 98%, and the marginal presence of 1% Portland show what type of product makes up the delivered volume. Cemsuisse links this development to demand for more environmentally friendly solutions, innovation and investments to reduce CO2 emissions. The connection with the Confederation's climate policy is explicit in the press release, not an interpretation added from outside.
The third dimension is logistics. With 68% of supplies by road and 32% by rail, road transport was the prevailing channel in the January-September period. The explanation provided by the sector concerns the difficult conditions of single-wagon transport: companies are forced to use trucks. The problem identified is not attributed to the quality of the cement or to demand, but to the organization of freight transport by rail.

## Key facts - AI-related goods → semiconductors and servers - Trade in these goods → 67% compared with the same period in 2025 - Share of global growth → 47% - WTO forecast → from 1,9% to 3,9% - First six months of 2026 → merchandise trade grew by 3,5% - Energy → oil -24%; liquefied natural gas -47%; global decline of 6% and 1% - AI investment in 2027 → growth of at least 30% - 2027 forecasts → trade 4,1%; GDP 2,6% this year and 2,9% next year
## WTO updates the forecast
Trade in artificial intelligence-related goods recorded a 67% increase this year compared with the corresponding period in 2025. Semiconductors and servers contributed 47% of the expansion of the global market, prompting the World Trade Organization (WTO), based in Geneva, to raise its annual growth forecast from 1,9% to 3,9%.
Director-General Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala outlined the revision in a note released on Thursday. She acknowledged the multilateral trading system's ability to adapt to turbulence, while warning that the shock had hit some countries harder than others.
### From the trade surprise to energy
Merchandise trade grew by 3,5% in the first six months of 2026, exceeding expectations set in March. Chief economist Robert Staiger attributed the figure to the resilience of trade despite the war in the Middle East.
> “We were surprised that the war in the Middle East did not reduce global trade as much as we thought,” said chief economist Robert Staiger.
The energy trend was different: exports of crude oil from the Middle East fell by 24%, while those of liquefied natural gas declined by 47%. Thanks to increased supplies from other regions, the global decline remained at 6% and 1%, respectively.
The main driver remains artificial intelligence. Staiger said that the increase in trade in semiconductors and servers was greater than expected: a figure below 30% had been expected. For 2027, investment in AI infrastructure is expected to grow by at least 30%. Okonjo-Iweala nevertheless deplored the fact that access to these technologies is not equal for all states.
Regional prospects diverge: Asian exports are expected to post the largest increase, at 9,9%, ahead of those from the northern part of the American continent and Africa. Europe is expected to see a decline of 0,1%, while the Middle East could suffer a contraction of almost 18%. ## From the global forecast to a Swiss perspective

However, the source does not provide a figure for Switzerland: it discusses the global market, energy supplies from the Middle East, exporting regions and GDP prospects. The figure must therefore be read as an international indicator, not as an automatic change in salary, the cost of living or employment in the country.
### Three distinctions to keep in mind
The first concerns timing. The 3,5% describes the first six months of 2026; the 4,1% is a WTO forecast for world trade in 2027. The revision from 1,9% to 3,9%, on the other hand, concerns the estimate for the year. Putting these values on the same footing would produce an incorrect comparison between an already recorded figure and a forecast.
The second concerns the subject. The 67% measures the increase in trade in AI-related goods, while the 47% indicates how much that dynamic fueled growth in the global market. The 3,5% concerns trade in goods as a whole. These are related indicators, but not interchangeable.
| Interpretation | Source data | Limitation for the Swiss public | |---|---|---| | Time horizon | 3,5% in the first six months of 2026 | not a Swiss figure | | Forecast | 4,1% growth in world trade in 2027 | not a forecast for the cantons | | Regions | Asia 9,9%; Europe contraction of 0,1%; Middle East nearly 18% decline | not a breakdown of Swiss exports |
The third concerns geography. Asia, Europe and the Middle East have different prospects; the source does not translate those figures into Swiss exports. It does not report a decision by the Federal Council or the cantons, nor data from SECO, UST/BFS or BNS/SNB. It does not announce changes to the cost of living. item.description: Il TF respinge il ricorso di un padre divorziato.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The Federal Supreme Court rejects an appeal by a divorced father. - Custody of the children alternates between the parents. - No deduction of 9'000 francs per child. - Maintenance payments already deducted rule out double tax relief.
## Key facts - Place: Canton Lucerne - Authority: Federal Supreme Court - Amount: 9'000 francs per child - Custody: alternating - Official residence of the children: with the mother - Outcome: appeal dismissed - Reason: double relief not provided for by law
## The ruling in the Lucerne case A divorced father residing in Canton Lucerne with several children cannot obtain a health insurance premium reduction based on the flat-rate deduction for children that the compensation office denied him. The Federal Supreme Court dismissed the appeal and deemed the cantonal decision lawful. The case directly concerns riduzione dei premi della cassa malati, but the decisive issue is the relationship between maintenance payments already deducted and a second deduction.
According to the judgment published today, the man and his ex-wife care for the children in alternating weeks. The divorce judgment awarded custody to both parents and established alternating custody. The children’s residence is nevertheless with the mother, where they are officially registered. Expenses incurred during each custody period are borne by the parent with whom the children are staying at that time. The father also pays the mother maintenance, which also serves to cover part of the costs of health insurance and healthcare.
The parent already benefits from the deduction for maintenance payments made to his ex-wife; allowing one for the children as well would have resulted in double relief, which is not provided for by law.
The cantonal court linked this interpretation to case law on tax deductions for dependent children. It referred to the Federal Direct Federal Tax Act, which excludes additional deductions when deductions for maintenance payments have already been claimed. It did not consider it decisive that the father cares for the children in rotation and bears the expenses during the custody periods.
For applications for premium reductions, the review takes place as part of mass administration, with standardized and automated processing of case files. The Federal Supreme Court therefore considered the cantonal conclusions compatible with higher-ranking law and dismissed the appeal. Moreover, cantonal law does not establish who is entitled to the flat-rate deduction in cases of alternating custody. ## The practical issue: a single tax allowance for the children The Lucerne decision compares four facts that can coexist in everyday life but did not carry the same weight in calculating the tax allowance. The father pays maintenance, has the children stay with him every other week, bears the expenses when they are with him and has the children officially registered with their mother. The cantonal court and the Federal Supreme Court, however, focused the calculation on the deduction already linked to the maintenance payments and on the civil domicile.
| Element | Reading in the case | |---|---| | Maintenance payments made to the mother | Already deducted by the father | | Alternating custody | Not enough to add the deduction | | Expenses during custody periods | Borne by the custodial parent | | Civil domicile | With the mother, operational reference |
The criterion followed by the judges can be understood as follows: the maintenance contribution paid to the mother already contributes to covering health insurance and healthcare expenses. Recognizing the 9'000 francs per child as well would have resulted in the disputed double tax relief. Expenses paid directly during alternating custody did not alter this conclusion.
### The grey area identified by the Federal Supreme Court The highest judicial authority nevertheless pointed out an inconsistency in the cantonal reasoning. For practical reasons, the Cantonal Court used the children's domicile as shown in the residents' register. That same decision-making process, however, ruled out in-depth checks of the custody arrangements, even though those arrangements were governed by the divorce judgment. In other words, the document was used to determine the domicile and maintenance obligations, while the actual custody arrangement was not examined in the same way.
This observation did not result in the appeal being allowed. The Federal Supreme Court indicated that other solutions are possible, but confirmed that Lucerne law does not specify who is entitled to the flat-rate deduction when custody is alternating. The judgment therefore does not automatically grant the benefit to the parent who bears the expenses during their weeks.
The parallel with dichiarazione delle imposte remains an element of the cantonal reasoning: the Federal Direct Tax Act was cited to support excluding an additional deduction when maintenance payments have already been deducted. For the case at hand, the practical point is to distinguish the right to custody from the possibility of combining two deductions.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## How to check your own case To examine a decision on the reduction of premiums in a situation of alternating custody, it is advisable to reconstruct the facts in the same order in which they emerge from the Lucerne case. The aim is not to automatically add up all expenses incurred, but to understand which item has already been used for the deduction and which domicile was taken into account.
### Four practical steps
1. Retrieve the divorce judgment. In the case examined, the appellant submitted it to the court. From that document, the previous instance obtained information on maintenance obligations and the children's domicile, as well as the custody arrangements.
2. Distinguish maintenance payments from custody expenses. The contribution paid to the mother must be kept separate from the costs incurred directly during the weeks in which the children are in the father's or the other parent's care. The decision considers the maintenance payments already deducted and does not turn custody expenses into a second deduction.
3. Verify the civil domicile. The children are officially registered with the mother, and this information was used as a reference in the standardized processing of the applications. The domicile recorded by the residents' registration office therefore had a concrete bearing on the case.
4. Compare the decision with cantonal law. In Lucerne, the flat-rate deduction is 9'000 francs per child, but the law does not determine who is entitled to it in cases of alternating custody. The review must therefore focus on the determining income, the maintenance payments already claimed, and the reasoning of the compensation office.
### If the decision is challenged In this case, the process went from the compensation office to the Lucerne Cantonal Court and finally to the Federal Supreme Court. The judgment does not indicate an automatic entitlement for the parent who shares the weeks with the former spouse. Instead, it shows that the appeal must address the precise reason for the refusal: avoiding double relief.
Before assessing a challenge, therefore, it is useful to assemble the divorce judgment, the calculation of the determining income, and the decision received. The costs incurred during custody alone do not determine the outcome of the case examined.

## TL;DR - Switzerland ranks first in the IMD World Talent Ranking - Adjusted EU/EFTA gap: 1,1% lower - Third countries: 4,5% lower - Immigration via free movement of persons: 77%
## Key facts - ILO data period → 2015-2020 - IMD World Talent Ranking → first place - Global Talent Competitiveness Index → second place - Immigrant nursing staff in high-income countries → 19,6% less than non-immigrant colleagues - Adjusted salary of EU/EFTA nationals in Switzerland → 1,1% lower than that of Swiss nationals - Adjusted salary of third-country nationals → 4,5% lower than that of Swiss nationals - Permanent immigration through free movement with the EU/EFTA → 77% - Average unexplained gap in high-income countries → about ten percentage points
## Switzerland's leading position Switzerland has ranked first in the IMD World Talent Ranking for years and is second in the Global Talent Competitiveness Index. The OECD also ranks it among the most attractive countries for highly skilled workers in its Indicators of Talent Attractiveness. The wage data adds a less well-known element: holding a foreign passport has almost no impact on salary.
An ILO report finds that in many highly developed economies, immigrants earn lower wages than residents even with the same qualifications. Once education, professional experience, age, sector and place of work are taken into account, an unexplained difference of about ten percentage points remains on average. Women are disproportionately affected, and in high-income countries, immigrant nursing staff receive, on average, pay 19,6% lower than their non-immigrant colleagues.
Switzerland is an exception, especially compared with Denmark, the Netherlands, Ireland and Sweden: for people from the EU/EFTA, the adjusted wage gap is virtually nonexistent.
### The comparison between the ILO and SECO ILO data cover the period 2015-2020. The organization clarifies that no more recent, comparable international calculations are available.
For Switzerland, a more recent analysis by SECO is available. After adjustment, the equivalent salary of people from EU/EFTA countries is 1,1% lower, within the margin of statistical uncertainty. SECO writes:
> «The data suggest that, in general, people who arrived through free movement seek pay similar to that of Swiss citizens and are able to obtain it».
For nationals of third countries, the difference rises to 4,5%. SECO links it primarily to structural factors: qualifications obtained outside the EU/EFTA are not always comparable or valued in the same way, while language proficiency could play a role.
The source does not attribute the result to a special law against discrimination based on origin or nationality. The equal-treatment law in fact protects only against discrimination based on gender. The explanation given is the composition of immigration: about 77% of permanent immigration over the past 15 years came through free movement with the EU/EFTA. Many of those who arrived have a high level of education, comparable qualifications, speak a national language or work for international companies where English is the main language. For those considering new opportunities, the first point of comparison nevertheless remains in annunci di lavoro. ## From statistics to choosing a job The Swiss figure does not describe a rule that assigns the same salary to everyone arriving from abroad. Instead, it describes a market in which, after adjusting for education, work experience, age, sector and place of work, the gap between Swiss and immigrant workers becomes very small for the EU/EFTA group. The distinction from third countries is therefore necessary to interpret the figures correctly.
| Group | Adjusted result | Reading indicated by the source | |---|---|---| | EU/EFTA | 1,1% lower, within the margin of uncertainty | Requirements and salaries similar to those in Switzerland | | Third countries | 4,5% lower | Structural factors, qualifications and language |
### The correct comparison For a female or male worker, the practical consequence is not to use their passport as the sole parameter. The soundest comparison starts with the variables considered by the analysis: education, experience, age, sector and place of work. If these characteristics are comparable, the Swiss result indicates a very small disparity for people from the EU/EFTA. The same interpretation cannot automatically be applied to people from third countries, for whom the source describes a larger difference linked mainly to structural factors.
Here, the structure of immigration is decisive. Over the last 15 years, the free movement of persons with the EU/EFTA has accounted for about 77% of permanent immigration. According to the source, many of these people have a high level of education and qualifications that are relatively comparable in the Swiss labor market. Some already know a national language; others are employed by international companies where English is the main language. These factors help explain how talent attractiveness and a small wage gap can coexist.
The Swiss average may also be influenced by the salaries of highly specialized professionals and executives, which raise the overall figure. This does not erase the differences between individual profiles, but explains why the national figure should not be read as an individual promise.
Two levels remain that should not be confused. The ILO allows international comparison for the 2015-2020 period, while SECO offers a more recent analysis for Switzerland; however, the international organization points out the absence of new and comparable calculations. To move from the statistical average to your own salary document, you can consult the guide to busta paga svizzera.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## How to turn statistics into a comparison The source does not present an administrative procedure, a deadline, or a document to use to obtain a salary that is aligned. The concrete action for those who work or are looking for work in Switzerland is to build a comparison that does not conflate groups, periods, and qualifications. The following approach stays within the available data.
### Four steps 1. **Identify the comparison group.** Before interpreting a pay difference, distinguish people from the EU/EFTA from those from third countries. The source shows that the two results are not interchangeable; using a single average would erase precisely the distinction considered by SECO.
2. Separate observed salary and adjusted salary. Note whether the comparison takes education, professional experience, age, sector, and place of work into account. These are the factors indicated in the source: without this check, a raw difference does not show whether the passport actually had an impact.
3. Check qualifications and language. For qualifications obtained outside the EU/EFTA, comparability and recognition on the Swiss labor market are not always equivalent. Language proficiency could play a role. If the activity takes place in an international company, the reference to English as the main working language, an element mentioned by the source, must also be considered.
4. Separate the periods. Use the ILO data for 2015-2020 for the international comparison and the SECO data for the more up-to-date Swiss analysis, without presenting them as if they were the same series. The ILO notes that it does not have more recent calculations that are internationally comparable.
### What the reader can conclude The result of the verification should remain proportionate. International statistics describe an average gap; the Swiss analysis measures differences after adjustment. Neither data point alone offers a promise about every person’s salary. Instead, they offer a criterion for assessing an offer: ask whether the profile is comparable, which statistical group is relevant, and which period is being used.
This reading can support both the search for a job and the review of a proposal already received. It is advisable to keep the data on education, experience, sector, and place of work separate, because these are precisely the variables used to adjust the comparison. In this way, the reader avoids automatically attributing to nationality a difference that the source also links to qualifications or language.

## TL;DR - 217 companies in Swiss robotics - 109 directly produce robots - 87% have fewer than 100 employees - Approximately 7’000 jobs in the sector
## Key facts - Companies in the sector → 217 - Direct manufacturers → 109 - Spin-offs from ETH and EPFL → approximately 80% - Companies with fewer than 100 employees → 87% - Jobs → approximately 7’000
### A snapshot of the sector
217 Swiss companies are linked to the robotics sector, and 109 of these directly design and manufacture robots. The latest economic monitoring report published by Raiffeisen describes a rapidly growing ecosystem closely linked to university research. Drones, underwater robots, and medical and industrial applications are all part of the same snapshot.
In July 2026, in Geneva, humanoid robots from Geneva-based company RB Labs were among the audience at an AI summit. The episode belongs to the public dimension of the sector, while Raiffeisen’s data mainly measure companies, spin-offs and employment.
### From research to companies
More than half of the companies originate from Swiss universities and research institutes. The Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Zurich (ETH) and the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Lausanne (EPFL) play a central role: approximately 80% of university spin-offs active in robotics originate from the two institutions. This share directly links academic research to the creation of new business ventures.
### Drones, snakes and seabeds
Researchers at the University of Zurich aim to use unmanned systems to inspect pylons, bridges and cargo ships. The technologies can also be used in fires and to search for survivors. Roboa, a company founded at ETH Zurich, develops snake-shaped robots to inspect pipes and hard-to-access spaces. Tethys Robotics develops underwater robots to monitor offshore infrastructure and carry out other operations in marine environments.
The majority of companies in the sector are small in size: 87% employ fewer than 100 employees. Approximately 7’000 people are employed in the sector overall. This structure shows that Swiss robotics also includes specialized companies born from research, in addition to industrial applications.
In terms of financing, Switzerland stands out in the European landscape. The European Spinouts Report 2025 puts the venture capital raised by robotics spin-offs originating at ETH at approximately 785 million dollars, and the amount flowing into ventures linked to EPFL at approximately 508 million. Anyone observing the labor market can use annunci di lavoro nella robotica to verify how this research translates into concrete positions. ## Impact on employment and the economy
### An already high industrial density
The figure that speaks most clearly to those working in factories is density: in Switzerland, there are 29 industrial robots for every thousand employees in the manufacturing sector. The figure is higher than that recorded in France, Austria, Canada and China. The comparison shows that automation is already measurable in Swiss factories, not only in experimental projects.
### The tasks most exposed
According to the estimates contained in Raiffeisen's report, robotics could affect approximately one in three jobs in Switzerland in the future. To interpret the figure in practical terms, it is necessary to consider the activities performed, not only the sector indicated in the contract.
| Area | What the analysis indicates | |---|---| | Industry and construction | Greater potential for robotization | | Technical and operational tasks | Exposure for auxiliary roles, electricians, operators and metalworkers | | Assistance, care and support | More gradual adoption because of the high level of human contact |
The flow of capital confirms the variety of applications. Investments concern minimally invasive surgery and agriculture, including autonomous systems for weed control. In tests in Aargau, the robot trained with artificial intelligence eliminated 90% of weeds on the second pass. Robotics is therefore entering activities beyond manufacturing, with uneven effects on jobs.
### The labor shortage remains a separate problem
The report puts a limit on the idea that robots can automatically make up for the shortage of skilled labor. Among occupations characterized by a particular shortage of workers, only 17% also show above-average exposure to robotics. In activities involving extensive human contact, such as assistance, care and support for people, adoption is expected to be more gradual. According to the analysis, human skills will remain difficult to replace at least in the medium term.

The following procedure helps prepare an application or assess a possible move into an activity connected to the sector.

1. **Map your current job.** Write down the tasks you perform and compare them with the categories indicated in the study: support staff, electricians, machinery and plant operators, metalworking workers. Set yourself a personal deadline to complete this assessment before submitting the application, then update the evaluation for each new position.

This framework prevents reading the overall number of jobs as a guarantee for every profession. ## TL;DR - Raiffeisen raises its 2026 GDP estimate to 1,7% - For 2027, it confirms growth of 1,3% - 2026 inflation at 0,7%, versus the previously estimated 0,5% - The SNB could raise interest rates on 10 December
## Key facts - Location → St. Gallen - Institution → Raiffeisen - GDP 2026 → 1,7%, excluding the effects of major sporting events - Previous 2026 GDP estimate → 0,8% - GDP 2027 → 1,3% - Inflation 2026 → 0,7%, versus the previous 0,5% - Inflation 2027 → 1,1%, versus the previous 0,8% - Next SNB review → December 10
ST. GALLEN – Raiffeisen economists have significantly revised upward their forecasts for the Swiss economy and expect the Swiss National Bank (SNB) to soon end its zero-interest-rate policy.
In an analysis published today, the cooperative estimates that in 2026 gross domestic product (GDP), excluding the effects of major sporting events, will increase by 1,7%, compared with the 0,8% previously forecast. For 2027, however, Raiffeisen maintains its forecast of growth of 1,3%.
### The signals behind the revision
In the institution's view, the Swiss economy continues to recover and, so far, has been little affected by the war in the Middle East. Even the latest escalation of the conflict in September did not dent business confidence.
The picture was supported above all by second-quarter growth data, which came in stronger than expected thanks to the dynamism of the pharmaceutical sector. The upward revision therefore follows economic indicators considered more solid than previously expected.
Raiffeisen has also revised its inflation forecasts upward. For 2026, it forecasts a price increase of 0,7%, compared with the 0,5% previously indicated. For 2027, the expectation is 1,1%, compared with the previous 0,8%.
Specialists explain that the impact of high energy prices should last longer than hoped. Core inflation, on the other hand, is expected to rise as a result of the franc's weakening and greater pressure from abroad.
Hence the possibility that the SNB could raise rates as early as its next assessment of the economic and monetary situation, scheduled for December 10. Raiffeisen notes that the economy is operating close to its potential and that inflation remains within the bank's target range, between 0 and 2%. Between July 2025 and June 2026, almost 5'000 job postings related to artificial intelligence were published in Switzerland. Compared with the same period of the previous year, the volume increased by 32%. This figure is reported in the Swiss AI Jobs Report 2026 by Hochschule Lucerne, dedicated to the demand for AI professionals in the country.
The result is not confined to IT. Demand grew in all ten main areas of activity analyzed. Outside IT, the report also considers the finance and insurance sector, education and research, the chemical-pharmaceutical sector, trade and logistics, public institutions, engineering, industry, legal and business consulting, and healthcare. IT retains first place with 1'211 listings, while the sharpest increase was recorded among public institutions, where postings rose by 67%.
Curdin Derungs, author of the study, notes that the increase in AI-related positions in the public sector signals growing confidence among politicians and administrators in this technology.
Small and medium-sized enterprises generated 76% of the overall increase and account for 62% of all published positions. For Derungs, the technology is no longer limited to large tech groups: it is entering the processes and services of established SMEs.
### Profiles and regions
Almost 40% of postings concern Data Engineering and Machine Learning Engineering profiles, involved in developing data infrastructure and the operational functioning of AI models. The report also identifies opportunities for Product Owner, Manager and AI Consultant roles: these professionals are responsible for identifying uses of AI within companies and turning them into operational solutions.
The market favors experienced profiles capable of combining technical and strategic skills. Senior positions increased by 42%, while permanent junior jobs account for only 5% of the total. At regional level, Zurich accounts for 2'181 postings, equal to 45% of the national total. In Central Switzerland, there are between 100 and 140 offers per 100'000 inhabitants, compared with a Swiss average of 96; in the Canton of Lucerne, postings grew by 55%. The total number of job postings describes an expanding market, but it does not offer the same indication to everyone looking for work. A practical interpretation involves different questions: which sector is demand concentrated in, which role is being sought, what experience is valued, and where are the positions posted.
### From quantity to choice
For a technical profile, IT remains the main numerical reference. The increase in public institutions' listings, however, adds a second perspective: 67% measures the growth in listings, not their absolute volume. SMEs offer another way of interpreting the data: with 62% of positions and 76% of the increase, demand is not confined to large technology groups.

Product Owner, Manager and AI Consultant are linked to identifying business applications and implementing them. For those at the beginning of their careers there are opportunities, but the share of permanent junior jobs remains at 5%; for those with experience, senior positions have increased by 42% and the search is described as more challenging.
Geographic distribution also changes the picture. Zurich accounts for 2'181 listings, representing 45% nationally, while in the cantons of Central Switzerland the rate is between 100 and 140 offers per 100'000 inhabitants, compared with 96 nationwide. The Canton of Lucerne records an increase of 55%. The text places the incident at the pension fund's external provider.
The company immediately filed a criminal complaint. It also informed the relevant Confederation services, Publica and other customers. The communication therefore places the incident at an external provider that has dealings with multiple customers; the press release specifies, however, that no other federal service has a business relationship with that same company.
The Office of the Attorney General of Switzerland launched an investigation. At the same time, the company and the various Confederation services are checking which data are affected and to what extent Publica's data are involved. The review was still ongoing at the time of publication.
The source also reports that Publica informed the persons insured with it of the data leak, its consequences and the measures taken. These are the elements indicated by the source for those insured with the pension fund.

Social assistance in the Canton of Lucerne represents a fundamental pillar for residents who find themselves in a situation of temporary or prolonged economic difficulty. Handling requests requires detailed knowledge of locally established administrative procedures. ### Access conditions and requirements
The Lucerne social protection system requires compliance with rigorous parameters to verify the actual situation of financial difficulty of the applicant. It is not enough to be in a temporary economic crunch, but it is necessary to demonstrate the exhaustion of every other source of income or available asset resource. The competent offices analyze the overall situation of the family unit, taking into account the income, recognized expenses and movable or immovable assets registered to the individual members. Transparency in the declaration of each individual income element constitutes the essential basis for starting the investigation. Cantonal legislation defines the criteria according to which a person is considered in need of economic and social help, excluding those who possess margins of financial autonomy that have not yet been exploited.
On a practical level, the Social Assistance Act of the Canton of Lucerne of 1 January 2004 sets the intervention thresholds. For a single person, the basic subsistence requirement is established according to the guidelines of the Swiss Conference of Social Action Institutions (CSIAS), which for 2024 stands on average at 1,031 Swiss francs per month, to which housing costs and essential medical expenses are added.
Unlike what happens in the nearby Canton of Zurich, where housing subsidies follow fixed parameters for municipal bands, in Lucerne the examination of rents takes into account actual costs as long as they fall within the limits of local reasonableness. For example, a single-parent family unit with one child in the city of Lucerne must submit documentation that includes the last three pay slips, bank and postal account statements of all accounts for the last 24 months, the business contract and health insurance policies with the certificate of benefit if received.
The operational checklist for submitting the application includes: - Completed and signed application form - Bank and postal account statements (last 2 years) - Rental contract and last three rental receipts - Notification of unemployment tax or other income - Health insurance certificate with details of premiums

The collaboration obligations require the beneficiary to actively participate in the professional reintegration programs promoted by the cantonal office, under penalty of a reduction in benefits of up to 30% in the event of unjustified lack of cooperation. The practical analysis of the procedures for accessing economic support in the Canton of Lucerne highlights a subdivision of competences between the different administrative levels. ### The competent offices and the reference authorities
When dealing with an application process for social assistance, the first step is to identify the municipal or cantonal office competent for your domicile. The local administrative structure receives the documentation, examines the completed forms and conducts the knowledge interviews with the person concerned. The social workers verify each individual attached document, comparing it with the databases and information provided by the applicant during the official interview. In Lucerne, as in similar situations such as Zurich or Bern, municipal social services operate through a well-defined mandate. For a single person, the minimum basic requirement according to the regulations in force is set at approximately CHF 1006 per month, to which must be added the certified ancillary expenses for housing and the actual costs for compulsory health insurance, minus any cantonal subsidies on sickness insurance premiums.
